findings.element: The owner surface after the first-run flow: .b-shared, the primary bar button, and the foot stamp (render-b.js ownerSurface, lines 1216-1233; foot() line 467)
findings.problem: Drive the real first-run path — state=owner-empty, type '3 October 2026', press 'Set the day', press 'Add a moment' — and the brand-new project (Aisling & Tom, created two seconds ago, never shared with anyone) renders 'Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it', a foot stamp reading 'Updated 15 July 2026', and a primary button reading 'Get the link'. Nothing has been published; there is no link. Who can see this is the single most consequential fact on an owner's screen — the whole product is one person handing another a private plan — and on the one screen where a new owner meets it, it is a lie inherited from the demonstration plan. The code already carries the correct copy ('Only you can see this' / 'Publish'), and the empty-state handler deliberately rewrites F.project.name, F.project.primaryDate and F.milestones — but never touches F.publication, so the unpublished branch is dead in the master and the entire pre-publish owner state is unproven. The empty state itself is careful about exactly this (it suppresses the stamp with foot({stamp:false})); one press later the care is gone.
findings.fix: In the add handler in states['owner-empty'] (render-b.js ~line 1327, beside the existing F.project.name / F.project.primaryDate writes) also write F.publication = { state: 'draft', publishedAt: null } and F.updatedLabel = F.fmt.medium(F.today) + ' 2026'. The three existing branches then render 'Only you can see this', 'Publish' and today's stamp with no further change. Then, in the 'publish' click handler (line 1062), on the first successful Copy the link set F.publication = { state: 'published', publishedAt: F.today } so the verb and the strap flip once, and add a fourteenth state 'owner-draft' so the unpublished owner surface has a frame and the behaviour gate can assert it.

findings.element: The 'Behind you' rail in state=day, opened (behindBlock({clock, back:true}), the .b-item[data-crowded] leader at b.css:227)
findings.problem: This is the screen the whole audience opens on the wedding morning, and its one piece of substance is illegible. Open the disclosure at 390: eight past rows run on a linear 274-day scale over ~640px, so six of the eight come back data-crowded=true with pushes of 21, 56, 91, 112 and 147px. The result is a knot of six ticks inside 100px at the top of the rail and then three rows — 'Final dress fitting' (42), 'Send the invitations' (56), 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' (63) — with no mark anywhere near them; the 63-day row's tick sits 141px above its own words with three other rows' words in between. The leader that is supposed to repair this is drawn ON the rail (left:-20px, 1px wide, fore-46 to fore-16) while the rail itself is a 1px white-16 line, so six overlapping leaders read as one slightly brighter stretch of rail and trace nothing. Below that, 170px of rail carries nothing at all between 'The Orchard reserved' and 'We said yes'. The count travelling with the words was the right half of the round-7 decision; the true-pixel tick is the half that fails here, because at 2.3px per day the past has no legible positions to be true to. Neither the owner's Behind-you nor the printed sheet draws this rail, so the fix is contained to one state.
findings.fix: In place() (render-b.js ~line 250), when back===true stop deriving top from away*px. Space the past rows evenly at their natural row height, keep each tick on its own row, and let the numeral in the gutter carry the distance — it already states '14 days back' in words and in the accessible name, so the past stays measured rather than listed. Keep the true-pixel scale for the future measure only, where 79 days over the same height is legible. Drop the .b-item[data-crowded]::after leader from the back rail with it; with one tick per row there is nothing left to lead.

findings.element: The +7 / +1 steppers and the .b-two measure column at >=1024 (state=owner-editing at 1440x960)
findings.problem: At 1440x960 the edited row 'Send the invitations' sits at y=696. One press of '+7' puts it at 822, a second at 948 with the viewport 960 tall, a third at 1074 and a fourth at 1200 — and scrollY stays 0 through all of it. The owner keeps pressing a control whose whole purpose is to move a thing along a scale, while the thing has been off the bottom of the screen for three presses. Below 1024 this does not happen: the page follows (scrollY 760 -> 890 -> 994 -> 1092) and the steppers hold still because the editing sheet is position:fixed. Round 7 refused 'scroll the measure to follow a move at desk width' on the grounds that the steppers do not hold still under a page scroll and Delete ends up under a repeat-press point — that objection is correct and this fix does not touch it, because the page is not what should move. The left column is already .b-stick; making the measure its own scroller moves only the right column, and the steppers, Done and Delete never shift by a pixel.
findings.fix: At >=1024 give the measure column of .b-two its own scroller — max-height:calc(100vh - <bar+strap height>); overflow-y:auto; overscroll-behavior:contain — and in setAway(), after place() runs, call scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on the edited .b-item against that scroller rather than the window. The left column, the editor, the steppers and the undo bar stay exactly where they are; only the rail moves under the moved moment. This also removes the 2130px document at 1440 that currently has no reason to scroll.

findings.element: The replacement .b-empty block written by the setday handler (render-b.js ~line 1362): countBlock(away) + .b-when + .b-emptyBody
findings.problem: The second screen a new owner ever sees — after typing a date and pressing 'Set the day' — shows '79 / days' at display size and 'Saturday 3 October 2026' underneath, and states today nowhere on the page. No 'Today is 16 July', no 'Today, 16 July', no indigo today rule; there is no indigo on the screen at all. Every other surface in this product anchors its dates twice, and round 7 refused deleting even one of the two statements precisely because unanchored time is a defect a prior round already paid for. It has come back in the one state you can only reach by driving, on the screen whose entire content is a date and a distance the reader is being asked to feel. '79 days' from an unstated now is arithmetic, not a feeling — which is exactly the argument the horizon was built on.
findings.fix: In the 'next' block built at render-b.js ~line 1362, insert the horizon's own two nodes between .b-when and .b-emptyBody: the indigo today rule (h('div.b-todayRule')) and h('p.b-todayLine', { text: 'Today is ' + F.fmt.dayMonth(F.today) }), using the same classes horizon() uses so the ramp, the leading and the rule's colour are inherited rather than restated.

findings.element: The 'add' branch of wireOwner (render-b.js line 1017-1045) and the 'A moment was added.' live-region line
findings.problem: 'Add a moment' picks a day for the owner by a rule nobody can see — seven days before the nearest future moment, floored at tomorrow — announces only 'A moment was added.', and lets the horizon immediately assert the invented date as fact. On the demonstration plan, five consecutive adds land at 9, 2, 1, 1 and 1 days away: three untitled moments piled on tomorrow, and the left column now reads 'Nothing is planned until 17 July' about a day the owner never chose. On a new project the rule is different again (halfway to the day), so the first moment an owner ever creates is dated 'Tue 25 Aug' out of nowhere and the horizon says 'Nothing is planned until 25 August'. Someone who has never used a tool of this kind reads a date in the WHEN field as a thing they entered. The plan is a record of decisions; the one action that creates a record should not manufacture a decision.
findings.fix: In the add branch, leave the new moment undated: create it with date:null, render its row at the foot of the measure under a 'No day yet' rule rather than on the rail, open the editor with the WHEN field empty and focused after the title, and make 'Done' refuse to close until a day is typed or stepped, reusing the three refusal sentences the empty state already ships ('Type the day first. For example, 3 October 2026.'). Change the remembered line from 'A moment was added.' to 'A moment was added. It has no day yet.' so the live region says the same thing. The horizon's gap sentence already derives from the dated items, so it will stop naming a day nobody set.

biggestWin: The horizon. One number, set at display size, with the ceremonial date under it and the unit whispered in mono beside it — '79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Wedding day' — is a genuinely original answer to what a plan for one day is, and it survives everywhere it is asked to: it is the whole phone screen, it is the unfurl card in a WhatsApp thread before anyone taps, it is the top of the A4 keepsake, and it degrades on the morning itself into the single word 'Today' without breaking its own grammar. Someone who has never used a project tool reads it in under a second with no training, which is the entire brief. Nothing else in the suite has a device this strong, and the surrounding restraint earns it: three colours, two weights, an empty state that asks one question and then stops asking, and copy that tells the truth in the two places it costs most ('Nothing has been deleted.', 'The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.'). What stands between this and 9.5 is not the resting screens, which are at the Linear and Vercel bar already — it is that the paths only reachable by driving are a round behind the frames. The first-run path is a half-day of work: two lines to stop a private plan claiming it is public, two nodes to put today back on the screen after the day is set, and one honest default for a new moment's date. The past rail on the wedding morning and the measure that lets the moved moment fall off the screen at desk width are builds rather than polish, and small ones: one branch inside place() and one scroller on the right column. All five are decisions already made elsewhere in the file and not yet carried through.
